questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false regarding primary biliary cholangitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Primarily involve large intrahepatic ducts
  • Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic autoimmune liver disease characterized by the progressive destruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts.
  • The disease primarily affects the small intrahepatic bile ducts, not the large ones.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 663,664

questions.stem: Which of the following statement are true regarding primary sclerosing cholangitis:

options.label: A
options.text: The most common antibody seen is pANCA

options.label: B
options.text: It is associated with ulcerative colitis

options.label: C
options.text: HPE shows circumferential onion skin fibrosis around the duct

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Primary sclerosing cholangitis is an immune mediated cholestatic disease. All the statements given above are true with respect to PSC. Hence, the correct option is D: All of the above.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 663,664

questions.stemHtml: A 54-year-old patient presented with jaundice( raised direct bilirubin) and the presence of a pANCA antibody. The liver biopsy is shown below. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis
  • The given clinical scenario with a histopathological image of liver biopsy showing onion skin fibrosis is suggestive of  primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 663,664

questions.stem: All of the mentioned antibodies are seen in type 1 autoimmune hepatitis except
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti LKM 1
  • Anti-LKM 1 antibody is not seen in Autoimmune hepatitis type 1. It Is seen in Type 2 autoimmune hepatitis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 651
